note: The two copies carry entirely different content under the same section number: A is the ability-to-repay/qualified-mortgage section, B is the higher-priced mortgage appraisal section.
A includes later amendments (prepaid account and hybrid prepaid-credit card carve-outs, Reg E cross-reference updates) that B lacks; B is the 2010-era text with footnote placeholders.
A reflects Dodd-Frank/CFPB-era amendments (RESPA/FIRREA authority, new mortgage sections, enforcement text, section 1029 exclusion) that B, which stands at its 2010 text, lacks.
Only capitalization of State, 'part' versus 'regulation', and a trailing citation differ; the rule is the same.

A has the Dodd-Frank high-cost mortgage rules (HOEPA expansion, open-end coverage, ability-to-repay cross-reference) while B retains the 2008 higher-priced loan formulation tied to the old section 32 triggers.
A includes later amendments (paragraph (a)(4) on permissible collection of HMDA and small business lending demographic data) that B lacks.
B has the added automobile-dealer-as-original-creditor example from a 2011 amendment, which A lacks (A has a single example).
A has later prepaid account and hybrid prepaid-credit card amendments and updated Reg Z cross-references and statute section number; B is the older text.

A limits coverage to entities under the AGENCY's prudential supervisory authority (banks), whereas B covers entities under the CFPB's GLBA rulemaking authority with the Dodd-Frank exclusions and FERPA provision.
B adds the CFPB-style coverage, with the section 1029 exclusion and a different OMB number, while A is the older Federal Reserve text without these; the substantive rule is otherwise the same.
